name: Question 19
problem:
Find the intervals where the function $F(t)=f(t)\cdot g(t)$ is differentiable, given that
 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\sqrt[3]{t-2}\,i+{2}^{t+1}\,j+\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)\,k, \\ g(t) & =\sqrt{t-1}\,i+({t}^{2}+1)\,j+{t}^{4}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
The function $F(t)=f(t)\cdot g(t)$ is differentiable over the common domain where both $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are differentiable. A vector function is differentiable if and only if each component is differentiable.

Let's now find the intervals where each of the functions $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are differentiable.

For the function $f(t):$ 

- The first  component $\sqrt[3]{t-2}$ is differentiable on $(-\infty ,2)\cup (2,\infty ).$

- The second component, ${2}^{t+1}$ is differentiable for all values of $t.$

- The third component $\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)$ is differentiable on $(-1,\infty ).$

So,  the intersection of the domains of all three components of $f(t)$ is $(-1,2)\cup (2,\infty ).$  

For the function $g(t):$ 

- The first component $\sqrt{t-1}$ is differentiable on $(1,\infty ).$

- The second and third components, ${t}^{2}+1$ and ${t}^{4},$ respectively, are differentiable for all values of $t.$

Hence,  the intersection of the domains of all three components of $g(t)$ is  $(1,\infty ).$    

Finally, the common domain of differentiability for $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ is 

$$
[(-1,2)\cup (2,\infty )]\cap (1,\infty )=(1,2)\cup (2,\infty ).
$$

Question 19

Find the intervals where the function F(t)=f(t)⋅g(t) is differentiable, given that f(t)=t−23i+2t+1j+ln⁡(t+1)k,g(t)=t−1i+(t2+1)j+t4k.

a
(1,2)∪(2,∞)
b
 (−∞,2)∪(2,3)
c
 (1,2)
d
 (−2,∞)
e
(−1,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function F(t)=f(t)⋅g(t) is differentiable over the common domain where both f(t) and g(t) are differentiable. A vector function is differentiable if and only if each component is differentiable.

Let's now find the intervals where each of the functions f(t) and g(t) are differentiable.

For the function f(t):

  • The first component t−23 is differentiable on (−∞,2)∪(2,∞).

  • The second component, 2t+1 is differentiable for all values of t.

  • The third component ln⁡(t+1) is differentiable on (−1,∞).

So, the intersection of the domains of all three components of f(t) is (−1,2)∪(2,∞).

For the function g(t):

  • The first component t−1 is differentiable on (1,∞).

  • The second and third components, t2+1 and t4, respectively, are differentiable for all values of t.

Hence, the intersection of the domains of all three components of g(t) is (1,∞).

Finally, the common domain of differentiability for f(t) and g(t) is [(−1,2)∪(2,∞)]∩(1,∞)=(1,2)∪(2,∞).
